documents.title: Dogwood Reserve | Messaging & Positioning Questionnaire
documents.text_excerpt:
MESSAGING & POSITIONING QUESTIONNAIRE

Brand Story
Origin Story:
How did your business start?
Alina Stevens purchased the property in approximately September 2025. It was called Abbey Manor at the time and was briefly renamed Meriwether Manor before the team chose Dogwood Reserve—a name that better suited the property and was easier for guests to remember. What began as Alina’s desire to create a family farm where her father could live and work expanded into a family-operated wedding and event venue centered on hospitality, connection, and the natural beauty of the land.

What inspired you to enter the wedding industry?
Alina’s original goal was not specifically to enter the wedding industry. She wanted to create a farm where her father could live, work, and continue doing what he loved. As the vision for the property grew, the team recognized that its expansive landscape, existing event spaces, and natural beauty could become a meaningful place for weddings and other celebrations. Savannah’s longstanding interest in event planning and the team’s shared passion for service helped shape that opportunity into Dogwood Reserve.

Can you share a memorable moment or milestone that defines your brand's journey?
A defining milestone has been transforming the newly purchased property into Dogwood Reserve: giving it a name that better reflects the land, renovating the getting-ready suites and key venue features, and developing the Terrace as a new event space overlooking the pastures. This marks the transition from an existing property with prior venue names into a new family-led brand and guest experience built around privacy, natural beauty, and hospitality.


Mission and Vision:
What is the core mission of your wedding business?
To provide a private, welcoming countryside setting where couples, families, and organizations can gather for meaningful celebrations, with the space, flexibility, and thoughtful service to focus on what matters most. For weddings specifically, the mission is to help couples create a day that reflects their vision while feeling comfortable, cared for, and at ease.

How do you envision your role in creating unforgettable wedding experiences?
Dogwood Reserve’s role is to provide both the setting and the support for a wedding day that feels unhurried, personal, and seamless. The property allows the day to unfold naturally in one place: spacious suites for getting ready, multiple ceremony settings, nearby cocktail-hour options, the Grand Pavilion for dinner and dancing, and an optional Honeymoon Suite at the end of the night. The team’s role is to pair that flexibility with warm Southern hospitality so couples and their families feel welcomed, comfortable, and able to focus on the celebration.


Values and Beliefs:
What core values drive your business?
Faith, family, hospitality, service, hard work, relationship-building, stewardship of the land, flexibility, and a commitment to making people feel welcome. The team also values authenticity, community, attention to detail, and creating a peaceful setting where people can connect and celebrate what matters most.

How do these values influence your interactions with couples and their families?
These values should make couples and families feel genuinely welcomed, listened to, and cared for from the first inquiry through the event day. The team aims to communicate clearly, treat the couple’s wedding as the meaningful occasion it is, and use its service-industry experience to anticipate needs and help everyone feel comfortable and at ease. Couples receive room to make the celebration their own, along with a venue team committed to preparing the property and supporting a smooth experience.


Ideal Client -  Who Specifically Do You Serve?
Ideal Client Profile:
Describe your ideal bride or couple. 
The current ideal-client profile is a laid-back, nature-loving couple seeking a private countryside wedding within reach of Atlanta. They are drawn to wide-open spaces, horses, rolling pastures, and a celebration that feels relaxed, romantic, elegant, and authentic rather than formal or urban. They likely fall within a mid-range budget and care about receiving strong value: the entire property, multiple event spaces, large getting-ready suites, tables and chairs, and twelve hours of access. They may enjoy some DIY personalization and want flexibility in their vendor choices, while still valuing optional professional support. This is a strategic starting point and should evolve as Dogwood Reserve books and hosts more weddings.

What are the common characteristics of your most satisfied clients? 
Because Dogwood Reserve is newly operating under its current ownership, there is not yet enough booking history to describe proven characteristics of its most satisfied couples. The current working hypothesis is that the best-fit couples will be laid-back, considerate, responsive, and excited by the property’s natural setting and flexibility. They will appreciate privacy and hospitality, respect venue policies and timelines, communicate openly, and value the experience of having the full property rather than expecting a highly urban or traditional ballroom environment.



The Offer + Problem/Solution
Problems/Solutions
What are their wedding planning priorities? 
Their priorities are creating a relaxed, meaningful celebration in a beautiful natural setting; having privacy and exclusive use of the venue; keeping the day cohesive in one location; making guests feel comfortable and welcomed; and having the flexibility to personalize the wedding without being forced into an overly rigid package. They are likely to value strong overall value, ample included space, practical logistics, and a team that helps the day feel calm and seamless.

documents.title: 2026-09-09 - Strategy Call - Ridgefield - Summary
documents.text_excerpt:
Quick recap
The meeting focused on updates and collaboration regarding the transition of website pages, Google and Meta Ads, and LeadLock processes. Whitney confirmed that all ads were now pointing to the new weddings page and discussed the ongoing migration of LeadLock landing pages to the new website with Amy. They talked about issues with the LeadLock mobile app and how Scott preferred using the desktop version. Whitney and Scott reviewed how lead information and form responses were being handled in LeadLock, ensuring that both Scott and Delia received necessary notifications. They discussed a new market research survey for couples who book, which Whitney would build in LeadLock, and reviewed potential improvements to the pricing guide brochure. Whitney also mentioned plans to potentially revamp the reporting format for ads and asked for Scott’s feedback on the current reports. The conversation ended with confirmation of their next meeting and a brief discussion on reporting preferences.

Next steps
Scott
Check with Val regarding the LeadLock mobile app issues and the recommended fix (reinstall and login with new credentials).
Think through and decide on who will handle updating the pricing brochure (Canva document) and circle back with Amy if necessary.
Whitney
Build out the market research survey in LeadLock and notify Scott when it's ready.
Investigate LeadLock settings to ensure Delia is receiving form submission notifications.
Send the current month's ads report to Scott with a video walkthrough.
Explore and potentially revamp the reporting format for future reports, starting possibly with the next month's report.
Summary
Website Traffic Migration Update
Whitney confirmed that all Google Ads and Meta Ads now direct traffic to the weddings page of the new website. She reported collaborating with Amy to move various LeadLock landing pages, including tour booking and package pages, from the old website to the new one. Whitney explained that while the new website currently uses the weddings page for ads traffic, they plan to create a dedicated ads traffic landing page on RidgefieldWeddings.com in the future.

LeadLock Mobile App Troubleshooting
Scott and Whitney discussed ongoing issues with the LeadLock mobile app, where Scott prefers using the desktop version instead. Whitney suggested troubleshooting steps including reinstalling the app and logging in with the new .com login. They also addressed concerns about lead notifications, confirming that Delia's email receives form submissions, including responses to scheduling questions, ensuring better team visibility when she returns from maternity leave.

LeadLock Contact and Survey Updates
Whitney and Scott discussed LeadLock functionality, specifically addressing how to handle a contact named Sophia Eaker who had opted out of text messages but would continue receiving emails. They reviewed market research questions that could be sent to couples after booking to better understand client preferences and buying behavior. Scott approved the research questions, and Whitney agreed to build them out as a professional survey in LeadLock, with implementation options to be determined later.

Canva Pricing Brochure Update
Whitney and Scott discussed updating the Canva pricing brochure to make it a stronger sales tool by including more detailed information about menu options and what's included in different wedding packages. They agreed that the current process of providing the pricing guide after lead capture should remain in place, with the website offering initial pricing information before requiring an opt-in for the full guide. Scott agreed to think through whether to handle the brochure update internally or engage Whitney's team, and they confirmed their next meeting is scheduled for October 14th at 8 AM.

Ads Report Format Improvement Discussion
Whitney discussed the current ads report format with Scott and sought feedback on previous reports to identify opportunities for improvement. Scott requested to see different reporting methods compared side by side to help evaluate which format works better for him. Whitney agreed to test new reporting approaches starting with the October report and will gather Scott's feedback on the different formats.
